CacheControlNoStore.description: The response must not be cached. Every /api response depends on who asks, and probe responses on the moment.

CacheControlNoStoreUnlessEarly.description:
The response must not be cached. Sent by the API, so it is missing when the
shared front rejects a declared oversized body before the API sees it; a
413 isn't cacheable by default either.

ExpireSessionCookie.description: Expires the session cookie, whether or not the request carried one.

RequestId.description: Valid first incoming X-Request-Id value, or a random base32 ID when missing, empty or invalid.

SetSessionCookie.description:
The new session's cookie: __Host-session=<token>; Path=/; Max-Age=<the
absolute session limit in seconds>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax. The
token is 32 random bytes in base64url without padding; it appears nowhere
else, and script can't read it.

CardId.description: Hyphenated UUIDv7 with the RFC 9562 variant. Hexadecimal letters are case-insensitive.
CardId.name: id

Cursor.description: Opaque pagination token from a previous page's next_cursor. Pass the value unchanged. Omit or send an empty value for the first page. Invalid tokens return validation_error with cursor/invalid_cursor.
Cursor.name: cursor

Limit.description: Page size in canonical decimal form, without leading zeros, a plus sign, or whitespace. Omitted or empty values use 20. Malformed or overflowing integers return validation_error with limit/invalid_integer.
Limit.name: limit

RequestId.description:
Optional client-supplied request ID. The first value is reused unchanged only
if it contains 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens.
Missing, empty or invalid values are replaced with a random base32 ID without
rejecting the request. The selected ID is echoed in the X-Request-Id response
header and included in server logs.
RequestId.name: X-Request-Id

example.description: A specification for describing HTTP APIs.
example.title: OpenAPI

LearningCardInput.description:
JSON card content. Each field is NFC normalized and trimmed, then must be
1 to its maximum length in code points (see LearningCardInput). Omitted or
null fields are treated as empty and fail validation. Unknown JSON
properties, including the card's read-only created_at and updated_at,
are rejected with bind_error.

LoginRequest.description:
The account's email and password, canonicalized as at registration. Only
their presence and maximum lengths are validated; anything else that
doesn't match an account is invalid_credentials. Unknown JSON properties
are rejected with bind_error.

RegisterRequest.description:
The new account's email and password. The email is normalized to NFC,
trimmed and lowercased; the password is normalized to NFC but never
trimmed. Omitted or null fields are treated as empty and fail validation.
Unknown JSON properties are rejected with bind_error.

CrossOriginRequest.description:
A browser sent this unsafe request (POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE) from
another origin, as Sec-Fetch-Site or Origin shows. Requests from the
client app's own origin and from non-browser clients pass.

HeadInvalidInput.description: Invalid query parameters or card ID. No response body.

HeadNotFound.description: No card exists with this ID. No response body.

HeadPayloadTooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the 1 MiB limit. No response body.

HeadProbeOK.description: The probe succeeded. No response body.

HeadProbeUnavailable.description: The instance should not receive traffic. No response body.

HeadSuccess.description: The corresponding GET succeeded. No response body.

HeadUnauthenticated.description: The request carries no valid session. No response body and no WWW-Authenticate header.

HeadUnexpectedError.description: An unexpected server or storage error occurred. No response body.

InvalidCardId.description: Path ID is not a hyphenated UUIDv7 with the required variant.

InvalidCreateInput.description:
Malformed JSON, incompatible JSON types and unknown fields, including
the card's read-only created_at and updated_at, return bind_error. Empty
bodies and invalid field values return validation_error.

InvalidCredentials.description:
The email has no account or the password is wrong; the response doesn't
say which. No WWW-Authenticate header is sent.

InvalidLoginInput.description:
Malformed JSON, incompatible JSON types and unknown fields return
bind_error. A missing or overlong email or password returns
validation_error with required or max_length.

InvalidQuery.description: Invalid query parameters return validation_error with field errors. Malformed or overflowing limits report invalid_integer; out-of-range limits report out_of_range; invalid cursor tokens report invalid_cursor.

InvalidRegistrationInput.description:
Malformed JSON, incompatible JSON types and unknown fields return
bind_error. Empty bodies and invalid field values return
validation_error: email reports required, max_length, invalid_format or
taken (an account has the email); password reports required,
invalid_characters, min_length or max_length.

InvalidReplaceInput.description:
An invalid path ID returns validation_error with id/invalid_uuid7 before body binding. Malformed
JSON, incompatible JSON types and unknown fields, including the card's
read-only created_at and updated_at, return bind_error. Empty bodies and
invalid field values return validation_error.

NotFound.description: No card exists with this ID.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the 1 MiB limit.

ProbeUnavailable.description: The instance should not receive traffic. No internal details are exposed.

Unauthenticated.description:
The request carries no valid session: no session cookie, or one whose
session is unknown, ended or expired. No WWW-Authenticate header is sent:
cookie sessions have no registered scheme.

UnexpectedError.description: An unexpected server or storage error occurred. Internal details are not returned.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: A nonempty request body was sent without Content-Type application/json.

CardId.description: Canonical lowercase, hyphenated UUIDv7 with the RFC 9562 variant.

Email.description:
The account's email in canonical form: NFC, trimmed and lowercased, with
one @ and text on both sides. Length is counted in code points. It is
the login name, and it isn't verified.

errors.description: Per-field failures, included only for validation_error responses.

code.description:
Card fields (title, description) report required or max_length.
Registration reports required, max_length, invalid_format or taken
(email) and required, invalid_characters, min_length or max_length
(password); login reports required or max_length. Query parameters
report invalid_integer or out_of_range (limit) and invalid_cursor
(cursor). Path IDs report invalid_uuid7 (id). untrimmed and
not_normalized are reserved: fields are canonicalized before
validation, so these codes are not currently returned.

created_at.description:
When the card was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, from the
database's clock. Read-only: request bodies don't take it.

updated_at.description:
When the card was last changed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, from
the database's clock. Equals created_at until the first update, and
changes with every update. Read-only: request bodies don't take it.

LearningCardInput.description:
Length constraints apply to the canonical form of each field: NFC
normalized, with leading and trailing white space removed, counted in
Unicode code points. Clients should validate that form. The server also
accepts untrimmed or non-NFC input and canonicalizes it before validation
and storage, so stored and returned values always satisfy the constraints
as written.

description.description: Card description. Length is counted in code points of the canonical form.
description.example: A specification for describing HTTP APIs.

title.description: Card title. Length is counted in code points of the canonical form.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque pagination token; null on the final page. Pass this value unchanged
as the cursor query parameter to fetch the next page. Clients must not
parse, construct, or rely on the token's format.

LoginRequest.description: Field errors: email and password report required or max_length.

password.description: Checked only for being present and at most 128 code points, so a stricter rule for new passwords never locks out an account.

RegisterRequest.description:
Length constraints apply to the canonical form of each field, counted in
Unicode code points: the email NFC, trimmed and lowercased, the password
NFC only. Clients should validate that form; the server canonicalizes
before validating. Field errors: email reports required, max_length,
invalid_format or taken; password reports required, invalid_characters
(a control character or U+FFFD), min_length or max_length.

email.description: One @ with text on both sides. Must not belong to an account.

password.description: Any printable characters, spaces included, from 15 to 128 code points. Kept as typed apart from NFC.

expires_at.description:
When the session expires unless it is used, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in
UTC. Each use extends it by the idle timeout, up to the absolute limit
after the session's creation.

SessionId.description:
Canonical lowercase, hyphenated UUIDv7 with the RFC 9562 variant. It names
the session; only the token in the session cookie authenticates.

UserId.description: Canonical lowercase, hyphenated UUIDv7 with the RFC 9562 variant.

sessionCookie.description:
The session token that registration and login set. The browser sends
it; script can't read it.
sessionCookie.name: __Host-session

info.description:
Backend API for accounts, sessions and learning cards.

Sessions are carried in the __Host-session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure,
SameSite=Lax, Path=/), which registration (POST /api/users) and login
(POST /api/sessions) set and logout (DELETE /api/sessions/current)
expires. The token never appears in a response body. An operation whose
security lists sessionCookie needs a valid session and answers 401 with
code unauthenticated without one; a failed login answers 401 with code
invalid_credentials. Neither sends WWW-Authenticate, since cookie
sessions have no registered scheme. The learning card operations don't
require a session yet.

Unsafe requests (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) that a browser sends from
another origin, judged by Sec-Fetch-Site or Origin, return 403 with code
cross_origin_request. No /api response may be cached: every one
carries Cache-Control: no-store.

Requests with JSON bodies must use Content-Type: application/json
(type and subtype are case-insensitive; media-type parameters are accepted).
Other or missing Content-Types on a
nonempty body return 415 with code unsupported_media_type. Titles,
descriptions and emails are normalized to Unicode NFC and trimmed
before validation and storage, and emails are lowercased; passwords are
normalized to NFC but never trimmed. Length limits count Unicode code
points after this sanitization.

Request bodies are limited to 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB). Oversized bodies
return 413 with code payload_too_large, whether the size is declared in
Content-Length or only discovered while reading a chunked body.

Every response includes X-Request-Id, reusing the incoming header when
provided or generating an ID otherwise. /api and unknown /api/* paths return 404
with code not_found. Unsupported methods on the collection return 405
with code method_not_allowed and Allow: GET, HEAD, POST; unsupported methods
on an individual card return 405 with Allow: DELETE, GET, HEAD, PUT.
Deeper paths below a card return 404.
info.title: Ludustudii API

get.description:
Returns cards ordered by descending UUIDv7 ID (newest first), using
keyset pagination. Pass next_cursor from the preceding response to
retrieve cards with smaller IDs. The cursor need not identify an
existing card. An empty limit or cursor is treated as omitted.

items.title: OpenAPI

200.description: A page of cards; items is an empty array when no cards match.

head.description: Executes the list operation with the same query validation, without a response body.

201.description: Card created. The body contains its ID and Location contains its relative URL.

Location.description: Relative URL of the newly created card.

204.description: Card deleted successfully. No response body.

head.description: Executes the get operation with the same ID validation, without a response body.

put.description: Both fields must be supplied. This operation does not create a missing card. The last write wins, whatever the client read before.

204.description: Card updated successfully. No response body.

put.summary: Replace a learning card's title and description

post.description:
Creates a session for the email and password and sets its cookie.
The session the request carried, if any, is deleted, so a token
planted before the login is worthless after it. An unknown email and a
wrong password get the same 401 invalid_credentials.

201.description: Logged in. The body is the session; Location is the current session's URL.

delete.description:
Deletes the session the request carries and expires the session cookie.
Succeeds without a session too.

post.description:
Creates an account and logs it in, as POST /api/sessions does: the
response sets the new session's cookie. The response reveals whether
an email has an account (taken).

201.description: User created and logged in. The body is the user; Location is the current user's URL.

get.description: The user whose session the request carries.

head.description: Executes the get operation, without a response body.

/livez.description:
GET and HEAD are supported. Other methods return 405 with the shared JSON
error body (code method_not_allowed), Allow: GET, HEAD, Cache-Control:
no-store and X-Request-Id. The global 1 MiB body limit runs before probe
handling and rejects oversized declared bodies with 413.

get.description: Checks no dependencies, including the database. Succeeds whenever the process can answer HTTP, including during draining.

head.description: Checks no dependencies, including the database. Succeeds whenever the process can answer HTTP, including during draining. HEAD sends no body.

/readyz.description:
GET and HEAD are supported. Other methods return 405 with the shared JSON
error body (code method_not_allowed), Allow: GET, HEAD, Cache-Control:
no-store and X-Request-Id. The global 1 MiB body limit runs before probe
handling and rejects oversized declared bodies with 413.

get.description: Pings the database with a one-second timeout. Returns 503 when the ping fails or the instance is draining for shutdown.

head.description: Pings the database with a one-second timeout. Returns 503 when the ping fails or the instance is draining for shutdown. HEAD sends no body.
